characters.name: Cannonball
characters.debutIssue: Marvel Graphic Novel #4: The New Mutants
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Kentucky coal miner's son who propels himself at high speed inside an invulnerable field. Has served with the New Mutants, X-Force, the X-Men and the Avengers. Agents are advised to stay out of his flight path.

characters.name: Sunspot
characters.debutIssue: Marvel Graphic Novel #4: The New Mutants
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Brazilian heir who absorbs solar energy for strength and heat. Has led the Avengers and taken control of A.I.M. Agents are advised that he can pay for lunch.
characters.notes: Infobox lists several teams; the five with real tenure are kept.

characters.name: Wolfsbane
characters.debutIssue: Marvel Graphic Novel #4: The New Mutants
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Scottish-born mutant who shifts between human, wolf and hybrid forms. Raised by a strict minister, she has served on five rosters. Agents are advised not to call her a dog.
characters.notes: Infobox cites 'The New Mutants (September 1982)', i.e. the graphic novel. Teams chosen from a longer list.

characters.name: Mirage
characters.debutIssue: Marvel Graphic Novel #4: The New Mutants
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Cheyenne mutant who projects a target's deepest fears or desires as illusions. Has led the New Mutants and served as a Valkyrie. Agents are advised to keep their thoughts tidy.
characters.notes: Page title is Danielle Moonstar; listed as Mirage (also Psyche, Moonstar) in comics.

characters.name: Karma
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Vietnamese refugee who can take control of other minds. Was among the first students of the New Mutants. Agents are advised to decline her offers to drive.
characters.notes: MCU snippet for Thor is an unrelated quote. Gender: identifies as female (a noted lesbian character); some versions of 'Shan' are her twin.

characters.name: Magma
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Roman-descended mutant from the lost Nova Roma who controls lava and heat. Has served the New Mutants and the X-Men. Agents are advised against asking about the volcano.
characters.notes: Alignment has swung between hero and villain (Hellfire Club, Hellions) but is most commonly hero.

characters.name: Warlock (Technarch)
characters.caseNote: Subject is a shapeshifting Technarch alien that can turn into machines and weapons. Escaped his father and joined the New Mutants. Agents are advised to speak slowly and literally.
characters.notes: Infobox flagged unreliable but title page is Warlock, correct character. Technarch is a techno-organic alien species; origin alien vs synthetic is contestable. Gender other: Warlock is a male-presenting being with no gender in the human sense.

characters.name: Cypher
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mutant who instantly translates any language or code. Was a founding New Mutant and long-time partner of Warlock. Agents are advised to leave a translator's bill unpaid at their own risk.
characters.notes: Infobox debut field was empty; New Mutants #13 (March 1984) from the article. Character was killed and later resurrected.

characters.name: Domino
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mercenary whose mutation bends probability in her favor. Has served as an operative with X-Force and Six Pack. Agents are advised not to play her at cards.
characters.notes: Infobox lists an impersonation by Copycat in The New Mutants #98 (Feb 1991) and herself in cameo X-Force #8 (Mar 1992), full appearance #11 (June 1992). Cameo-as-herself used. Alternative: New Mutants #98 / 1991-02. X-Men team could be argued. Domino in Deadpool 2 (Fox) does not count.

characters.name: Deadpool
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mercenary with a regeneration factor and a documented disregard for the fourth wall. Has served with X-Force, the Avengers and Heroes for Hire. Agents are advised not to engage in conversation.
characters.notes: Origin mutate (Weapon X experiment activating healing factor; infobox 'Human mutate'). Some sources classify as mutant. Alignment antihero vs hero. Reynolds in Deadpool & Wolverine; Fox films do not count.

characters.name: Shatterstar
characters.caseNote: Subject is a gladiator from Mojoworld, bred to fight with twin swords. Is a veteran of X-Force and a part of the Krakoan era X-Men. Agents are advised not to call him by his gladiator name at the dinner table.
characters.notes: Origin: Mojoworld-born genetically engineered; infobox lists species as Mojoworlder or similar; alien used though he is described as a mutant's offspring in some versions. MCU: Lewis Tan as Rusty / Shatterstar in a cameo in Deadpool & Wolverine. Real name: Gaveedra-Seven, 'Ben Russell' is his Earth alias.

characters.name: Warpath
characters.caseNote: Subject is an Apache mutant with superhuman strength, speed and senses, and the brother of the late John Proudstar. Has been a steady member of X-Force. Agents are advised to take a seat rather than argue.

characters.name: Boom-Boom
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mutant who generates explosive spheres of energy. Has operated under several codenames across X-Force, the New Mutants and Nextwave. Agents are advised not to hand her anything round.
characters.notes: Page title is Tabitha Smith.

characters.name: Rictor
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Mexican mutant who generates seismic vibrations. Has served with X-Factor and X-Force. Agents are advised to hold the tremors until after the meeting.
characters.notes: Infobox alliances empty; teams taken from article body.

characters.name: Strong Guy
characters.caseNote: Subject absorbs kinetic energy and rechannels it as physical strength. Has been a long-standing member of X-Factor. Agents are advised not to hit him.

characters.name: Multiple Man
characters.caseNote: Subject creates duplicates of himself by taking a physical impact. Serves as a private investigator with X-Factor Investigations. Agents are advised to count heads before dismissal.
characters.notes: Origin: mutant (X-gene) vs mutate (powers triggered by a childhood accident). The character is classified as a mutant in Wikipedia. Changed to mutant; see notes. Defenders membership is minor.

characters.name: Siryn
characters.caseNote: Subject is a sonic-scream mutant, the daughter of Banshee, with a famous temper. Has served on X-Factor Investigations and X-Force. Agents are advised against asking her to keep it down.
characters.notes: Real name given as Theresa Rourke Cassidy; Wikipedia article says Theresa. Page uses 'Tracy Cassidy' as an alias spelling.

characters.name: Hope Summers
characters.caseNote: Subject is the first mutant born after M-Day, widely hailed as a messiah. Raised in the future by Cable, she later led her own squad. Agents are advised to avoid the topic of destinies.
characters.notes: Cover dates differ in some sources; Wikipedia gives November 2007.

characters.name: Quentin Quire
characters.caseNote: Subject is an Omega-level telepath and telekinetic from the Xavier Institute. Led a student uprising before turning into a Phoenix host. Agents are advised not to dismiss him.
characters.notes: Alignment is contested between antihero and villain early on, hero later.

characters.name: Pixie
characters.caseNote: Subject is a British mutant who teleports through pixie dust and wields magical soulsword. Rose from the student body to the X-Men. Agents are advised to wear a jacket against the sparkles.
characters.notes: Origin is mutant (X-gene) with later magic ties (Cstep). Teleport via pixie dust, soulsword gained from the Cat of Cimmeria; magic aspects secondary.

characters.name: Armor
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Japanese mutant who creates a psionic suit of armor around herself. Joined the X-Men as a student at the Xavier Institute. Agents are advised not to push her.
characters.notes: Infobox resolved to Iron Man in infobox file; read from the correct article via search (Astonishing X-Men #4, Oct 2004). Young Avengers membership has been questioned; verify. Names matched in MCU snippets are for the word 'armor', not this character.

characters.name: Blink
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mutant who opens teleportation portals and fires them as weapons. First appeared in the Age of Apocalypse. Agents are advised to count the exits.
characters.notes: Original Age of Apocalypse version; later mainstream Marvel version is a different history.

characters.name: Chamber
characters.caseNote: Subject is a British mutant who unleashed psionic flame through his chest and jaw. Was a founding Generation X student. Agents are advised to watch how he speaks.

characters.name: Husk
characters.caseNote: Subject is Cannonball's sister who sheds her skin to reveal a new material underneath. Has served with the X-Men and X-Force. Agents are advised to double-check which Paige they are talking to.
characters.notes: Teams from article; Generation X membership short; X-Men teams chosen as primary.

characters.name: Marrow
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mutant with a bone-growing ability and a radical past with the Gene Nation. Later joined the X-Men and Weapon X. Agents are advised to avoid hugging.
characters.notes: Debut as Sarah in Cable #15; as Marrow in X-Men Prime (July 1995). Used first appearance as Sarah.

characters.name: Maggott
characters.caseNote: Subject is a South African mutant with slugs in his abdomen that digest matter. Was a member of Generation X and the X-Men. Agents are advised not to ask about lunch.
characters.notes: Infobox gives the year 1997 only; April 1997 is the cover date per issue records. Verify month.

characters.name: Cecilia Reyes
characters.caseNote: Subject is a New York doctor who produces a protective force field. Joined the X-Men reluctantly. Agents are advised to take her medical advice.

characters.name: Doop
characters.caseNote: Subject is a green floating creature who speaks a language no one has translated. Worked with X-Statix and X-Force. Agents are advised to disregard the thumbs-up.
characters.notes: Origin and gender are contested; 'other' used since gender is unstated and the character is treated as a genderless entity. Gender: male in some sources.

characters.name: Fantomex
characters.caseNote: Subject is a French thief and Weapon Plus product with a living ship, E.V.A. Has served as an operative of X-Force. Agents are advised that he will steal the silverware.
characters.notes: Origin: super-soldier (Weapon Plus) vs mutant (lighter claim). Per rubric, Weapon Plus counts.

characters.name: Captain Britain (Brian Braddock)
characters.caseNote: Subject is a British physicist who received a mystic amulet from Merlin and Roma. Has served with Excalibur, MI-13 and the Illuminati. Agents are advised to say please.
characters.notes: Origin: magic (amulet of Merlin) vs tech vs cosmic. Betsy Braddock's own Captain Britain role is a different subject.

characters.name: Meggan
characters.caseNote: Subject is a shapeshifter who mirrors the emotions of those around her. Member of Excalibur and spouse of Brian Braddock. Agents are advised to keep their moods in check.
characters.notes: Origin contested: mutant (empath shapeshifter) vs other; 'mutant' is the common Wikipedia label. Real name Meggan Puceanu is given in one source only; none in infobox.
